sections.body:
This is a story about Hà. She is eight years old and she is curious about everything.

Behind the hill at the end of her street there is a path she has never walked. On that path there is a **castle**. Hà can see it from her window: grey walls, one round **tower**, and a gate with a small slot in it.

Nobody in her street talks about the castle. Her mother says only one thing about it: come with empty hands.

Hà thinks about this for three days. What does empty hands mean? No toys, no phone, no snacks? Just her and her hands.

A good adventure has a shape. It has a beginning, a middle and an end. The beginning tells you who is going and why. The middle brings the surprise. The end gives you something worth keeping.

This day has that shape. At the beginning, Hà walks up the hill with nothing in her hands. In the middle, three rooms each ask one small thing of her. At the end, a great door opens, and the castle gives something back.

Read it slowly. Then tell it to someone else. That is how an adventure becomes yours.
examples: This story is about a girl who spends one day in a castle.
A good adventure has a beginning, a middle and an end.
I can tell this story again tomorrow.
sections.heading: What this castle day is about

sections.body:
On the fourth morning, Hà walks up the path.

She leaves her sandals by the gate. She leaves her water bottle in the grass. Her hands are empty and her heart is beating fast.

The slot in the gate is the size of a coin. It is not a **keyhole**. A keyhole is a hole where a key goes in to open a lock. This slot is too small and too round for a key.

Hà puts her hand flat over the slot. The stone is warm, like a cup of tea in the morning.

Then the gate opens by itself, slowly, and it makes no sound at all.

Inside is a hallway with a stone floor. On the walls hang three doors: a red one, a blue one and a green one. Above the green door is a small **garden** sign with a flower on it. Above the red door there is a cooking pot. Above the blue door there is an open book.

A voice that comes from everywhere and nowhere says: "One room at a time. And mind the middle door."

Hà looks at the middle door. There is no middle door. There are three doors. She decides to start with the red one, because she is hungry.
examples: She left her sandals and her bottle by the gate.
The stone of the gate was warm like a cup of tea.
One room at a time, said the voice.
sections.heading: How the castle appeared

sections.body:
The red door opens on a kitchen. A big pot is on the fire, and the soup is nearly ready.

"Stir it," says the voice. "That is all."

Hà stirs. The soup is hot and heavy, and it smells of ginger and sweet potato. She stirs for a long time until her arm aches. When she stops, the soup has turned into something bright orange, and the smell fills the whole castle.

"Now eat some," says the voice. "Somebody else will want it too."

Hà eats one spoonful. Then she ladles a second bowl and leaves it on the table. It will be here when the next child comes.

The blue door opens on a library with shelves that go up to the ceiling. One book is glowing softly.

"Read one page," says the voice. "Out loud."

Hà reads. It is a story about a mouse who wants to see the sea. When she reads the last word, the book stops glowing and becomes an ordinary book again.

"Keep one thing from this room," says the voice.

Hà wants to keep the book. She looks at it for a long time. Then she takes one pressed flower from the shelf. The book stays on the shelf where it belongs.

The green door opens on a garden. It is night inside, with a round moon over the flowers. An old woman in a green coat is waiting there.

"Plant one seed," says the old woman. "And give it water. But take nothing with you when you leave."

Hà plants the seed. She gives it water. She wants to dig it up and take it home, but she keeps her hands in her pockets instead.
examples: She stirred the soup until her arm ached.
She left the second bowl on the table for the next child.
She took one pressed flower and left the book on the shelf.
sections.heading: The middle: three rooms, three small rules

sections.body:
The garden gate opens and Hà is back in the hallway. In front of her is a door she has not seen before. It is much bigger than the other doors.

There is a slot in it, the same shape as the slot in the gate outside.

"Put in the thing you love most," says the voice. "Only that. And you will not get it back today."

Hà puts her hand in her pocket. There is exactly one thing in there. A small brass **key** on a red string. It is the key to her grandmother's old house, and her grandmother is inside that house right now.

Her hand shakes. She thinks about keeping it. She thinks about the small grey key on the ring. She thinks about the door it opens, the one that smells of rice and old wood.

Then she takes it out. It is warm in her palm. She puts it into the slot.

The key disappears with a sound like a bell. The great door swings open, and light comes out of it, warm and golden, and Hà walks in.

Inside the room there is one table. On the table there is a small clay pot with a green shoot coming out of it. A seed from the castle garden. And beside it, a grey cat with very calm eyes.

The cat purrs. Hà lifts the pot carefully, and holds it against her chest.

The next morning, her grandmother's key is on the kitchen table, polished bright. The castle took it for a day. It gave back the seed and a friend.
examples: Put in the thing you love most, said the voice.
The key disappeared with a sound like a bell.
It gave back the seed and a friend.
sections.heading: The surprise: the great door and the little slot

sections.body:
These are the words you will meet in this story. Learn them here, and you can use them in your own sentences.

A **castle** is a big old building with thick walls, made to keep people safe. Castles usually have towers and gates.

A **tower** is a tall round part of a castle. You can climb to the top of a tower and look out over everything.

A **key** is a small metal thing that opens a lock. A **keyhole** is the hole where the key goes in.

A **garden** is a piece of ground where people grow plants and flowers. A garden needs water and a little care every day.

A **seed** is the small beginning of a plant. A seed is tiny and quiet, but if you plant it and water it, it grows.
examples: A castle has thick walls and a gate.
A key goes into a keyhole.
A seed grows if you plant it and water it.

sections.body:
What did Hà learn? She learned that the castle was not full of gold. It was full of small acts. Stir the soup. Read a page. Plant a seed. Each one was tiny, and each one was enough.

She also learned the hardest lesson of the day. The castle did not give to her. It gave to the child who came after. It gave back to her only when she let go of the thing she was holding tight.

Here is how to tell this adventure to someone. Keep the order, and the surprise will land in the right place.

Start with Hà at the gate with empty hands. Tell the three rooms in the middle, one door at a time. Save the great door and the little slot for last. Then say the small lesson in one short sentence.

The lesson of this adventure is this: your hands are empty at the start, and that is how they can be full at the end.
examples: The story starts with Hà walking up the hill with empty hands.
The surprise comes at the very end.
Your hands are empty at the start, and that is how they can be full at the end.
sections.heading: The small lesson, and how to tell the story
steps: Start with the character: Hà walking up the hill with empty hands.
Tell the middle: the red kitchen, the blue library and the green garden.
Tell the surprise: the great door, the slot, the key and the seed.
End with the lesson: your hands are empty at the start, and that is how they can be full at the end.

item.summary: Hà finds a castle that only appears to children who come with empty hands, and she spends one whole day inside it. Follow her through the kitchen, the library and the garden, and to the great door with the small slot. After reading, you can retell the day, use five new castle words in your own sentences, and explain what the castle gave back.
item.title: One Day in a Magical Castle
